item.title: 2026 KGM Musso EV review
item.description: The 2026 KGM Musso EV is the Korean company’s first electric ute in Australia, but can it live up to its past?

item.title: Honda revises EV strategy after posting fourth straight quarterly loss
item.description: Honda is changing up its EV strategy in the US and China in response to wildly different market conditions, and continuing losses.

item.title: Ford Ranger and Everest recalled
item.description: Ford is once again recalling its Ranger and Everest for an issue that may see them suddenly shift into Park at low speeds without illuminating the brake lights.

item.title: Toyota LandCruiser FJ baby off-roader to get HiLux diesel, chance for Australia – report
item.description: The baby FJ was ruled out for Australia as it only offered an older petrol engine – but reports of a diesel version mean it could come here.

item.title: Smarter leasing made easy with FleetPartners
item.description: SPONSORED: Why more small businesses are choosing business-ready leasing with a FleetPartners Fully Maintained Operating Lease.

item.title: Tesla Australia moves to subscription-only model for Full Self-Driving
item.description: If you want to pay the full up-front $10,100 cost to add Full Self-Driving (Supervised) to your Tesla, you'll need to do so by March 31.

item.title: Chevrolet Corvette Z06 Bathurst edition revealed for Australia
item.description: A hard-core 300km/h road-going special to commemorate the Corvette’s debut at this weekend’s Bathurst 12 Hour has been unveiled.

item.title: 2026 Suzuki e Vitara Australian specs revealed, new EV offers up to 426km of range
item.description: Suzuki's first EV in Australia will come in two model grades with up to 426km of range, but prices are still unknown.

item.title: Gone in 20 seconds: The $200 Toyota steering wheel lock fails the grinder test
item.description: Can a $200 steering wheel lock stand up to a cheap grinder for more than 20 seconds? Only one way to find out...

item.title: 2026 Kia EV9: Hot GT arrives as Korean brand's priciest model ever
item.description: The Kia EV9 GT will be over $8000 more expensive than the current flagship EV9, but it brings a big bump in performance plus electronically controlled suspension.
